This template describes a standard workflow for analyzing single cell PNA data using the `pixelatorR` package in R. It covers data loading, quality control, clustering, annotation, abundance, proximity, optional statistical testing, and optional single-cell graph visualization.

**Important:** Users must actively review and adjust quality control thresholds, select markers, and most critically, perform manual cell type annotation based on marker expression patterns. Automated annotation provides a starting point but should always be verified and refined through careful inspection of differential abundance patterns and marker distributions.

**How to run interactively:** Open and run the numbered notebooks in `modules/` in order (`01` through `04`; `05` and `06` are optional). Start with `01_quality_control.qmd`.

**How to re-render everything:** Render this file when you want a single HTML report of the full workflow at the end of a project (requires [Quarto](https://quarto.org/)).

**Where to edit:** Steps that depend on your experiment are labeled **Decision checkpoint** in each module. Search for **Decision checkpoint** in the module you are running.

## Project Folder Structure

```
.
├── data/
│   ├── metadata.csv
│   └── *.pxl
│
├── modules/
│   ├── common_setup.R                 # Shared setup (sourced automatically)
│   ├── 01_quality_control.qmd
│   ├── 02_clustering_annotation.qmd
│   ├── 03_abundance.qmd
│   ├── 04_proximity.qmd
│   ├── 05_statistical_testing.qmd     # Optional
│   └── 06_cell_visualization.qmd      # Optional
│
└── results/
    ├── checkpoint_data/               # Saved between modules
    │   ├── pg_data_merged.rds         # After module 01 (QC-filtered)
    │   ├── selected_markers.rds       # After module 01
    │   ├── annotated_seurat_object.rds # After module 02
    │   └── markers_to_test.rds        # After module 02
    ├── 01_quality_control/
    ├── 02_clustering_annotation/
    ├── 03_abundance/
    ├── 04_proximity/
    ├── 05_statistical_testing/
    └── 06_cell_visualization/
```

**Note:**

- All plots are saved in both PDF and PNG formats.
- Folder numbering (01–06) corresponds to the analysis modules.
